subject: Velocity spike: temporary throughput degradation — internal playbook + customer note
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, ops@fastcart.com
Date: 2026-12-18T03:12:00-08:00
Subject: Velocity spike: observed throughput drop on gen-api-prod (us-west1)

Team —

Quick summary: around 02:45 UTC we saw a sustained 30-40% drop in gen-api-prod throughput for BrightCart requests with a correlated rise in p95 latency (from ~280ms to ~820ms). The spike is concentrated on streaming endpoints and appears tied to increased rerun volume from BrightCart's nightly job.

What we've done so far:
- Identified a batch of long-lived streaming sessions from FastCart (their ops team confirms a retry loop).
- Shifted a subset of traffic to the secondary pool (manual route override) which recovered throughput modestly but left p95 elevated.
- Captured perf graphs and KV cache hit patterns (attached).

Immediate asks:
1) Karthik / eng: can you validate whether the recent kernel scheduling tweak (deployed 12/17) could cause tail blocking on streaming endpoints? Any quick revert or guard we can toggle?
2) Marissa / product: we need a short customer-facing blurb for ops@fastcart.com explaining mitigation steps and ETA for a stable fix. Keep it explicit about temporary workarounds.
3) Neha / CS: can you confirm BrightCart is willing to stagger their 02:00 UTC job by 30m while we stabilize? Ops contact is ops@fastcart.com.

Attachments: perf-graphs-20261218.png (latency / throughput over the last 6 hrs), bridging-runbook-v1.pdf (internal mitigations).

I recommend we avoid broad public comms until we confirm root cause; keep customer updates to ops@fastcart and the account team.

—Ben
Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T03:58:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Velocity spike: observed throughput drop on gen-api-prod (us-west1)

Thanks Ben — digging in now. Quick notes from initial triage:
- The 12/17 kernel scheduling tweak added an opportunistic work-stealing path intended to improve multi-tenant fairness. On paper it should be safe for streaming, but I do see contention on the per-GPU worker queues when sessions have long-lived KV sequences.
- Reproduction locally: with a synthetic long-tail streaming workload I can reproduce elevated tail latency when the KV eviction pressure and the scheduler both attempt aggressive stealing.

Immediate suggestion:
- Toggle the new scheduler to conservative mode on the affected pool (low-risk flip) and observe for 15 minutes. I'll prepare the toggle and run smoke tests. If toggling reduces p95, we can roll back the aggressive heuristic while we iterate on a more robust fix.

Customer messaging: we should be transparent but avoid deep technical jargon. Proposed short note for ops@fastcart.com (for Marissa to finalize):
"We observed a throughput degradation affecting streaming endpoints during your nightly job window. Our on-call SREs have applied a temporary configuration change which should stabilize performance. We're continuing root-cause analysis and will follow up with a timeline for a targeted fix. Recommended action: if possible, postpone non-critical batch retries by 30 minutes until we confirm stability. We appreciate your patience and are treating this as high priority"

I'll start the conservative toggle and post results in the Slack thread.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Software Engineer (Serving Runtime)
From: ops@fastcart.com <ops@fastcart.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T04:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Velocity spike: observed throughput drop on gen-api-prod (us-west1)

Thanks for the quick heads-up. Confirmed — our nightly reconciliation job did start retrying on multiple item failures around 02:40 UTC after a transient downstream error. We're able to push the job back 30 minutes; doing so now.

Request from our side:
- Can you share an estimated window for when performance will be considered stable? Our downstream workers have backoff logic but we want to avoid cascading retries.
- If you end up needing us to throttle the job programmatically (rate limit), we can add a short feature flag to the job to limit concurrency for tonight.

Appreciate the transparency. Please keep our CS lead Alice looped on substantive updates.

—FastCart Ops (on behalf of BrightCart)

Hi — Rachel from Redwood here (account lead for BrightCart). Thanks Ben and Karthik for the rapid response and thanks Ops for agreeing to shift the job. Quick consolidated status and next steps for clarity: 

Status now:
- Karthik toggled the scheduler to conservative mode on the affected pool at 03:18 UTC; we've observed incremental improvement in throughput and a drop in p95 from ~820ms to ~340ms in the interim graphs.
- Ben's team is monitoring; attached are the current perf screenshots and the internal runbook we've started following.

Customer-facing notes (for Ops / Alice):
- Short-term: Staggering tonight's batch by 30m is the right move — thank you. No other action needed unless you see cascading retries.
- What to expect: We anticipate a stable profile within the next 90 minutes as the conservative scheduler reduces queue contention. If we confirm stability, we'll leave the conservative mode in place and schedule a targeted fix next week that avoids the trade-off.

Action items (owners):
- Ben: keep monitoring for at least 2 hours and escalate if p95 rises over 500ms again.
- Karthik: open a follow-up INF ticket with the rollback details and a plan for a non-blocking scheduler improvement (target: next sprint).
- Marissa / Neha: prepare a short post-incident summary for the account (bullet points + timeline) and a proactive note for the CSM to send to Alice by EOD.

I'll draft the customer summary and post to the account thread in an hour; feel free to edit. Thanks all for the quick coordination — appreciate Ops adjusting their window.

Regards,
